name: sec-scene-depth-cap
title: Editor host security S2: nesting-depth cap for scene/prefab/snapshot JSON and a hierarchy depth limit in GameObject::Deserialize (audit F4)
acceptance: All Tests-workflow jobs green (8 checks; required linux (Release, x86_64, Clang)); Windows Debug leg proves the cap-1 tree is stack-safe

JSON nesting pre-check before parse on every untrusted scene/prefab/snapshot entry point (LoadScene, OpenScene, WritePlaySnapshot, play snapshot, RestoreSceneSnapshot, autosave, SceneFile::Load, prefab load)
GameObject::Deserialize has an explicit depth cap (>= glTF kMaxNodeDepth + margin) and fails the load with an error instead of overflowing
Tests: cap-1 loads, cap+1 and a 100000-deep chain are rejected without a crash, for Deserialize, LoadScene via the editor server and a prefab
No protocol change; F16 resolvers untouched; docs document the caps and why
notes: Security-sensitive (audit F4). The reviewer must try to break it: (1) find any scene, prefab or snapshot JSON entry point (client or disk) that still parses unchecked, including SceneFile::Load, autosave, edit history, the play child's snapshot and Model prefab JSON; (2) check that the pre-scan handles strings with escaped quotes and brackets, and nesting through component data, not only children; (3) check that a failed deep load leaves the open scene and the ReferenceResolver untouched and leaks nothing; (4) check that the hierarchy cap admits every model the importers accept (kMaxNodeDepth 256) under some parents; (5) look for any remaining recursive walk (Serialize, dump, operator==, json copy, SetScene, Find) reachable with a tree deeper than the cap, especially through SetEntityParent if (iii) was skipped, which must then be documented; (6) the deep test inputs must be built iteratively. The audit's example cap of 128 is deliberately not used: each hierarchy level costs 2 JSON levels, and imported models can be 256 nodes deep. Touches EditorServer.cpp at the LoadScene, OpenScene and snapshot sites only; expect a trivial merge with sec-host-dos-limits (ServerLoop and Send, other functions) and on docs/testing.html. May run in parallel with sec-host-dos-limits and sec-lua-budget.
